baseline:
B
A standard transformer block is composed of two main sub-layers: a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a position-wise fully connected feedforward network (MLP).

B
An MLP is defined by its structure, which includes an input layer, an output layer, and at least one hidden layer in between. The use of non-linear activation functions (like ReLU or sigmoid) in these hidden layers is crucial, as it allows the network to learn complex, non-linear relationships in the data.

B
The MLP, also known as the Feed-Forward Network (FFN), takes the context-aware embeddings produced by the attention mechanism and applies a non-linear transformation, allowing the model to process the information more deeply.

C
The MLP's weights are adjusted during training to map specific input patterns (keys) to desired output patterns (values). This process allows the network to store factual knowledge by learning the association between a concept and its related information, effectively acting as a key-value associative memory.

C
The knowledge or "facts" a neural network learns are encoded in the numerical values of its parameters. The training process is the systematic tuning of the weights (W) and biases (b) to store patterns from the data.
